text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS
- President Arpad Goncz yesterday released his detailed reasons for rejecting two prominent bills last week.

- Foreign Minister Laszlo Kovacs met Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat in Bethlehem yesterday. Earlier Kovacs had talks with Israeli Foreign Minister David Levy and the two signed an inter-governmental agreement on technical cooperation.
- The coalition consultative council met to discuss current domestic policy issues. Free Democrat President Ivan Peto said the two parties differed only on the privatisation law amendment.

- Democratic Forum (MDF) President Sandor Lezsak said that MDF is asking the government to initiate a debate in the Council of Europe and the OSCE on the conflict between the Serbian Socialist government and the opposition.
- Laszlo Kekesi, the new president of the tax authority was installed in office yesterday.
- President Jacques Chirac of France will pay a state visit to Hungary on January 16-17.
- The European Union, in an economic projection made public Monday, expects Hungary's GDP to grow by 3.5 percent in 1997.
- The BUX Index started the new year with a rise of 156.98 points, hitting 4,291.29, driven by rises in some of last year's most active stocks.
- New Budapest police chief Attila Berta said yesterday that his staff will remove as quickly as possible those few policemen who are in contact with the underworld.
MAGYAR HIRLAP

- The Prime Minister had no knowledge of the state's plan to repurchase Polgari Bank, however this autumn Horn is said to have asked the finance minister to amend the Budapest Bank privatisation contract in favour of the ministry.
- Hungary will sign a free trade agreement with Turkey on Wednesday.

- Duties on the imported components of exported products will no longer be refundable from July 1, reports this paper. The reason is that Hungary will at that time join the pan-European co-prosperity zone.
- As of late December a total of 477,000 unemployed were registered by job centres.

- Tractebel, the Belgian owner of power plant Dunamenti Eromu Rt., will sell its 48.76 percent stake if this month's negotiations with the State Privatisation and Holding Co. regarding an energy price increase do not end satisfactorily.
- The State Privatisation and Holding Co. has begun setting up its third list of companies to be included in the simplified privatisation programme.

- The State Money and Capital Market Supervisory Office approved the introduction of T shares of retailer Skala-Coop onto the OTC market of the Frankfurt Stock Exchange and papers of the travel agency Ibusz to the OTC market of the Vienna Stock Exchange.
VILAGGAZDASAG
- Several foreign-owned banks started the new year with interest rate cuts on deposits.
NAPI GAZDASAG
- The central budget projects tax revenues of 1,508 billion forints this year.
- Despite a central budget subsidy of 60-62 billion forints last year, the Hungarian Railways suffered losses of 15 billion forints.
- The construction of terminal 2/B at Ferihegy airport is expected to start in February.
-- Budapest newsroom (361) 327 4040
